Phoenix is a test and simulation environment for electronic passports and eID cards. Phoenix Cloud connects the online simulator to the NFC interface of your Android phone.
Use the simulation directly in your browser at epassport-simulator.de.

Phoenix Cloud is an independently developed fork of the Android Smart Card Emulator (ACardEmulator) from vsmartcard by Frank Morgner and contributors. Phoenix additions include cloud connectivity, pairing and the user interface (as of 14 October 2026).\n\nThe app continues under the original GNU General Public License, version 3 or any later version (GPL-3.0-or-later). Show a colored live log in this diagnostics window. Diagnostic events only; no credentials or APDU payloads. Up to 120 entries are held in memory.
Example screen from the Phoenix app
User will be loaded after connection

Sign in at epassport-simulator.de. Open Settings and Set up device. Scan the QR code or import the downloaded JSON file. Check the server in the confirmation dialog. The one-time code expires after ten minutes.

Unlock your phone and enable NFC. Tap Connect. Cloud reachable confirms the internet connection only. NFC readiness and actual transfers are shown separately. If needed, remove the case, check battery saver settings and keep the phone steady.

Choose Simulate card. In the online simulator, provide a synthetic eID or ePassport profile to your phone. Place the phone NFC antenna over the external card reader. Keep the phone unlocked and available. The reader starts communication. No real identity document data is required.

Choose Read card and hold an authorized NFC test card against the back of your phone. Keep the app open. Select the Android NFC reader in simulator settings and check the card. Card detection does not prove successful PACE or EAC authentication.

The separate diagnostics screen provides response times, interruptions and structured tests. Position guidance compares measured positions; it does not measure radio field strength. The authorized ADB companion connects the phone to the Mac and REINER SCT reader for laboratory tests. Compatibility reports are saved only after your explicit confirmation.

Move the phone, screen facing up, over the fixed reader/test card in steps of about 5 mm. Arrows guide a 3×3 grid; they do not sense a radio direction. Each position is compared over 30 seconds with at least 5 observations. No running test means no assessment.

You confirm a successful test and send the following to your paired Phoenix account: manufacturer, model, Android/API version, app version, tested mode and number of successful attempts. No serial number, IMEI, PIN, keys or card data. This is a user-confirmed observation, not official certification. Save now? Reader mode confirms an ISO-DEP SELECT/READ baseline, not PACE/EAC verification. Card simulation requires the complete recorded profile test to pass.
Compatibility report saved in your account.
Report not saved. Check cloud connection and test result.

The authorized Mac companion runs the selected test using the attached REINER SCT reader. USB debugging and the Phoenix laboratory debug build are required. The local USB test temporarily opens and configures the separate vsmartcard test app. Only synthetic profiles are used. Results and APDU metadata remain local initially. No compatibility report is submitted automatically. The baseline test mounts the selected synthetic cloud profile and repeats up to 120 measurement cycles. Position guidance stops it automatically after nine measured positions; stop it earlier at any time. The Mac companion must use the same synthetic Phoenix test account that this app is paired with.
